comments: http://thesaurus.weblio.jp/content/%E3%82%AC%E3%83%B3%E3%82%92%E9%A3%9B%E3%81%B0%E3%81%99 Both are creative ways of saying "she's glaring at me"; mixing in the literal meaning retains imagery and works just fine. First reminds of the crossbow, second of the Knife metaphor used around her multiple times in her route especially. (NOTE: knives may be catspeak.) -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The narrator dusts himself off while Kiri glares daggers at him, described with two Japanese glare idioms. The English adds dusting off pride and expands the idioms into an incoherent sequence of literal eyeball gunfire and mincing.
adjudicated.remedy: As I dust myself off, Kiri keeps shooting me vicious glares.
